text:
allen: Heads-up — after the driver rollout last night we're seeing a p99+ latency bump on short sequences. suspected interplay between kernel selector and KV cache invalidation. perf-bot alerted at 03:12 UTC.
perf-bot: ALERT: service=runtime p99 latency +28% vs baseline; region=us-west-2; signal=kernel-path-change
nora: ack. link to flamegraph? seen anything from the canary? :thinking:
samir: canary had small noise but nothing that big. I pulled a flamegraph from canary: short-seq paths show 2 extra kernel calls (fastattn -> fallback path) and a cache miss spike for seq_bin=0-16
allen: here's the kernel select log snippet from a problematic request:
```
[2026-03-17T03:09:12Z] kernel_select: model=gpt-small variant=qt8 arch=ampere seq_len=12 selected=fast_attn_v2 fallback=softmax_v1 kernels=[fast_attn_v2, softmax_v1] time_ms=0.18
[2026-03-17T03:09:12Z] kv_cache: lookup key=model:gpt-small:v=20260317:seqbin=0 prefix_hash=0x7f3 miss
```
chad: that prefix_hash miss is worrying. Did the driver change break key salting? We bumped the key format in v2.3.1 to include kernel_profile tag.
lisa: yes — driver added kernel_profile to cache key to avoid collisions across kernel choices. but we didn't persist-migrate existing cache entries. so older keys won't match -> cold misses -> extra kernel execution + p99 hit.
allen: that matches the timeline. so two impacts: (1) key mismatch -> misses; (2) kernel selector occasionally flips to slower fallback when cache miss causes different memory layout.
nora: quick mitigation: roll back kernel_profile addition for a short window and run a background migration script to copy old keys -> new keys, or salt namespace per model version then gracefully retire old namespace.
samir: migration plan I sketched:
```
# pseudo
scan cursor 0 match "model:gpt-small:v=20260316:*" -> for each key compute new_key = add_kernel_profile(key) -> copy key -> preserve ttl
```
samir: downside: double memory during migration and risk of race with live writes. we can do copy-if-not-exists and drop TTL recreation if exists.
lisa: alternative: maintain backward lookup in runtime: if miss on new key, try old-key decode then prime new key on hit. cheap and avoids mass copying.
allen: agree that runtime fallback lookup is simplest short-term. add metric to measure extra latency from fallback probe.
chad: long-term we want a stable key contract. kernel_profile in key is fine but needs versioned persistence and a migration matrix in releases.
nora: also saw weirdness with seqbin bucketing heuristics — new selector does a dynamic bin recompute that occasionally moves requests from seqbin 0->1 for sequences around boundary (len 16). that affects cache hit ratio.
allen: can we peg seqbin boundaries for 24h to stabilize metrics while we fix keys? set config: seqlen_buckets.override=true and boundaries=[1,16,32,64]
samir: I'll push a canary with pinned buckets + runtime old-key fallback probe. will measure p50/p95/p99 and cache hit rate.
perf-bot: NOTE: new canary deployed to us-west-2 at 03:32 UTC (config seqlen_buckets.override=true)
chad: also add a temporary metric: cache_key_probe_latency_ms and cache_key_probe_count. want graphs in grafana dashboard eng-runtime/kvcache
lisa: created dashboard panel draft and added alerts: probe_rate > 1% of get_rate -> notify eng-runtime
nora: after canary up, I saw p99 drop back ~15% within 5m. still above baseline but trending down. cache hit ratio for seqbin=0 went from 61% -> 87% with the fallback probe priming new keys.
allen: good. next steps:
- samir: keep canary for 6h, collect histograms and heap pressure during migration window
- lisa: finish dashboard + alerting
- chad: draft postmortem entry and long-term key contract doc (include migration example and release checklist)
- nora: coordinate with infra to plan a scheduled migration run if needed
lisa: for postmortem, include cost estimate of double memory during copy migration and CPU overhead for runtime probe hits.
samir: one more note — kernel selector heuristics: we should record selector_decision metadata into cache entries (kernel_hint) so future warmups favor same kernel path and avoid flip-flopping during cold misses.
allen: can we embed kernel_hint as a small tag in the cache value? yes, then on lookup if kernel_hint != current_selector then maybe prime with chosen kernel or trigger async re-eval.
chad: that reduces oscillation risk, nice.
perf-bot: RESOLVED in canary? status=partial; p99 still +12% vs baseline but improving; followup required
allen: thanks all. Samir — post your canary numbers here when you have 6h snapshot. we'll decide rollback vs full migration after that.
samir: will do. quick experiment note: local run with 200k reqs, pinned buckets, and runtime probe reduced extra kernel calls by ~68% and lowered average latency 9%.
allen: perfect. closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions spike. :thumbsup:
